newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe shares end week active but softer.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe shares end week active but softer.

text.p: Zimbabwean stocks were active but weaker on Friday, largely on the back of a loss in blue-chip conglomerate Delta, brokers said.
"The share market lost a few points largely due to a dollar loss in Delta which traded in large volumes," a broker said.

He added however that a poor subscription to a seven year government stock issue meant that interest rates on the local money market would remain low in continued liquidity and the bourse would still be more attractive to investors.
Other counters to lose on Friday included pharmaceutical group Caps, which came off 25 cents to 320, pork processor Colcom, 30 cents easier at 340 and cement firm Circem, which lost 35 cents to 815.
Publishers Zimpapers at 1,950 and another cement company Porthold which traded at 1,450, were both 50 cents easier while timber producer Border shed 150 cents to 1,100.
The 57-counter industrial index lost 30.60 points to 8617.73, but was 283.18 points firmer on the week.

In minings, coal giant Wankie added 50 cents to 550 and further five cent gains in gold miner Falgold and copper producer Mhangura pushed the seven-share index 24.80 points up to 1067.00. This was however a 6.31 point loss on the week.
